summary: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a sinologist and historian. Educated at the University of Königsberg (~1710–1716) and under Christoph Theodosius Walther, he held posts at Königsberg (~1717–1726) and as Professor at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (1726).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at King's College London, Heidelberg, and Freiburg (PhD ~1861–1862), he held posts at King's College London, Oriental College, and the University of the Punjab.

Gouriswar Bhattacharya specialized in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Alfred Bloch (~1963–1967) and served as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin (~1974–2000).

Govind Chandra Pande worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studying under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (~1943–1947). He served at the universities of Allahabad and Rajasthan, and chaired the Allahabad Museum (~1986) and IIAS (~2000–2005).

Govind Kumar Meena specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya and Banaras Hindu University before becoming an assistant professor at Government College University, Lahore in 2022.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye worked in Indology and sociology. He studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon, later heading the Sociology Department at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).

Govind Swamirao Gai was a scholar of Indology, epigraphy, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976) and later worked as a Consultant for Epigraphy at the American Institute of Indian Studies (attested 1986).

Govind Vinayak Devasthali worked in Indology and studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist. He held a professorship at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and later served as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).
Grace Constant Lounsbery was an American scholar of Buddhist studies. She studied at Bryn Mawr College (~1892–1896), founded Les Amis du Bouddhisme in 1929, and served as its president until 1964.

Grace Morley was an art historian and Indologist who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris. She directed the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (1934–1958) and the National Museum, New Delhi (1960–1966).

Grace S. Fong is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1978–1984). She served as a professor at Smith College (~1985–1988) and later as associate professor and department chair at McGill University (~1989).

Grace Sturtevant Hopkins was a linguist. She completed her undergraduate studies at Vassar College (~1920–1924) and earned her Ph.D. at Yale University (~1928–1932), where she studied under Edgar Howard Sturtevant.
Graeme MacQueen was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1972–1978) and served as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1974–2004).

Grafton Elliot Smith was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Sydney Medical School, the University of Sydney, and St John's College, Cambridge, and later held an academic post at University College London (~1919–1936).
Graham E. Clarke was a scholar in tibetology and related fields. He held positions at the Institute of Development Studies and served as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford (attested 1998).
Graham Lock is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes is a philosopher and Japanologist who earned his Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1979–2008) and later at University College Cork (~2008–2016).

Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge and the LSE under John Lane Bell. He held positions at the University of Melbourne and has been a Distinguished Professor at the CUNY Graduate Center since 2009.

Graham Sandberg was a scholar of tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1866–1870) and the Inner Temple (~1870–1874), later serving as a Chaplain for the Government of India (1885–1904).
